definitions.explanation: The money returned to you when you pay more than the price of something. The お is an honorific prefix that is typically included.

examples.japanese: お{釣|つ}りはいりません。
examples.notes: Polite way to let someone keep the change

examples.japanese: お{釣|つ}りは500{円|えん}です。
1000{円|えん}{出|だ}したら、お{釣|つ}りが300{円|えん}でした。
examples.english: When I paid with 1000 yen, the change was 300 yen.

examples.japanese: お{釣|つ}りをもらうのを{忘|わす}れたので、{店|みせ}に{戻|もど}らなければなりませんでした。
examples.english: I forgot to get my change, so I had to go back to the store.

notes:
お{釣|つ}り is almost always used with the honorific お prefix.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- お{釣|つ}りをもらう: to receive change
- お{釣|つ}りはいりません: keep the change
- お{釣|つ}りが{出|で}る: change comes out (vending machines)
- お{釣|つ}りを{間違|まちが}える: to give wrong change

AT STORES:
- お{釣|つ}りの{確認|かくにん}をお{願|ねが}いします: Please check your change
- お{釣|つ}りは○○{円|えん}です: Your change is ○○ yen

RELATED TERMS:
- {小銭|こぜに}: coins, small change
- {両替|りょうがえ}: money exchange
- {釣|つ}り{銭|せん}: change (formal)

With the rise of キャッシュレス{決済|けっさい} (cashless payment), お{釣|つ}り is becoming less common in daily transactions.
